name: DEUS Finance
rootCause: DeFi protocol Deus Finance was attacked by a flash loan, and hackers manipulated the price of the oracle machine and stole about $3 million, including 200,000 DAI and 1101.8 ETH through Tornado mixing.

descriptions.text: DeFi protocol Deus Finance was attacked by a flash loan, and hackers manipulated the price of the oracle machine and stole about $3 million, including 200,000 DAI and 1101.8 ETH through Tornado mixing.

DEUS Finance’s Fantom deployment was hit on 2022-03-15 by a flash-loan oracle manipulation that distorted a USDC/DEI price path, forced liquidations, and produced about $3 million in visible proceeds. The DEI lending path trusted a manipulable USDC/DEI spot price for liquidation decisions. A flash loan changed the pool reserve ratio inside one transaction, and that transient valuation was accepted as if it were durable market price.

On 2022-03-15, DEUS Finance’s Fantom lending market was exploited after a flash-loan-sized trade moved the USDC/DEI price used in solvency checks, letting the attacker trigger liquidations and extract about $3 million. DEUS let solvency and liquidation logic depend on a USDC/DEI AMM spot price that the same transaction could move. That coupled valuation to a manipulable pool state, so a temporary flash-loan-funded swap could distort the oracle input long enough to change liquidation outcomes.

Hackers were able to use a flash loan attack to manipulate a price oracle, pulling 200,000 DAI and 1101.8 ETH (totaling almost $3.1 million) out of the Deus Finance defi platform. PeckShield, the analysis firm that identified the vulnerability, wrote that the $3 million number represented the amount the hackers were actually able to withdraw and put through a cryptocurrency tumbler , but that the loss to the project may have been larger. The CEO of Deus Finance subsequently wrote on Twitter that users whose positions were liquidated as a result of the exploit would be repaid.
